mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weekly observations (-16.3 to -13.6 to -13.1 to -12.0). This monotonic recovery reflects accumulating behavioral momentum (routine re-establishment, confidence) that should persist unless disrupted, pushing the next 4-week mean higher than the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:three consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: If the next 4-week mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the last 4-week mean despite the prior 3-week upward run, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES jumped sharply from -20.6 to -13.7 in the most recent week, a single-week swing of nearly 7 points. If this crosses an implicit office-reopening threshold, it signals a policy-driven loosening of workplace attendance restrictions that will raise associated weekday retail footfall over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points week-on-week, crossing above -15
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -20.6 to -13.7 in one week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES jump above -15, the policy-driven reopening mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward simultaneously (TRANSIT -53.3 to -45.6; WORKPLACES -14.6 to -13.7 with intermediate dip), the joint recovery of commuting and office attendance compounds to drive retail foot traffic higher than either series alone would predict, via combined commute-linked shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show net improvement over the 4-week window
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue improving together, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined over the last two weeks (7.1 to 5.7), indicating reduced time spent at home. In an easing-restrictions regime, this behavioral shift away from home-bound activity frees time and intent for discretionary outings, supporting higher retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 7.1 to 5.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, the behavioral substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has risen steadily (1.3 to 4.7) indicating increased stock-up or essential-shopping behavior. If this exceeds a threshold increase, it suggests households are substituting concentrated grocery trips for broader discretionary retail outings, which would suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 5 points from baseline within a week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 1.3 to 4.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM crossing above 5 points, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is volatile (-32.4, -25.7, -30.7, -27.7), consistent with winter weather variability in Melbourne. When PARKS crosses above a less-negative threshold (indicating a mild-weather week), outdoor substitution reduces indoor retail visits, lowering RETAIL_REC in the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated between -32.4 and -25.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after PARKS crosses above -20, the seasonal substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved markedly across all four weeks (-53.3 to -45.6), a sustained trend reflecting gradual policy-driven relaxation of movement restrictions. This ongoing transit recovery is an always-on leading indicator that should continue to support higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as mobility normalizes.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean does not increase despite continued TRANSIT improvement, the always-on transit-led mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in WORKPLACES alongside a rise in RESIDENTIAL in the same week would indicate renewed caution or incipient restriction tightening, as seen partially in the t-2w to t-1w transition (WORKPLACES -19.6 to -20.6, RESIDENTIAL 6.9 to 7.1). This joint signal, if it recurs, predicts a near-term pullback in RETAIL_REC as households re-adopt home-bound behavior.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell and RESIDENTIAL rose together between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 2 weeks despite a joint WORKPLACES decline and RESIDENTIAL rise, the tightening-interaction mechanism is rejected.
